learningObjective: Explain why compiler passes over tensor IRs commonly functionalize in-place operations into non-mutating SSA-like forms.

canonicalClaims.claim: Functionalization rewrites in-place tensor ops into non-mutating equivalents, restoring single-assignment so that downstream passes (CSE, DCE, fusion, alias-free scheduling, autograd) can analyze the graph as pure dataflow.
conditions: The IR distinguishes mutating and non-mutating operator variants (as in ATen).
External mutation contracts (tensors that escape the compiled region) are honored via boundary copies where needed.
nonImplications: Does not imply that the emitted machine code cannot use in-place stores; the codegen may reintroduce mutation when analysis proves safety.
Does not imply that functionalization is always cheap; boundary handling for aliased/exported tensors adds bookkeeping.

sourceMappings.locator: SSA construction; benefits for dataflow analysis

misconceptions.claim: Functional (non-mutating) tensor operations execute faster at runtime than in-place ones.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Functionalization is an IR-level rewrite; runtime speed is determined by the emitted kernel, which can be in-place after analysis.

misconceptions.claim: In-place operations cannot be expressed in FX Graph or any tensor IR.
misconceptions.whyWrong: IRs can represent mutation; the issue is that mutation makes analysis harder. Functionalization is a convenience transformation, not a correctness necessity for representability.

misconceptions.claim: Functionalization is only needed for autograd tracing; a pure inference compiler does not need it.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Even for inference, fusion and scheduling passes benefit from SSA form; alias-free reasoning enables correct pattern rewriting.

misconceptions.claim: Functionalization always introduces additional runtime copies.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The IR pass renames values; codegen decides whether copies are needed. In many cases, the fused kernel writes to the same buffer as the input, avoiding copies.

implementationFacts: SSA: each name has exactly one static definition
Functionalization renames every mutating op result to a new SSA value
PyTorch AOTAutograd applies functionalization before Inductor lowering
performanceScenarios: Fusion across an in-place op requires proving the mutation does not alias any other live tensor; functionalization sidesteps this by making the pattern pure and letting bufferization/codegen decide storage reuse.
